chose: prose advisory reports divergence, not duplication: every pair is labeled IDENTICAL or DIVERGED and diverged ranks first, with only diverged pairs eligible for --raise
over: reporting all duplication (a summary legitimately restating a fuller argument would read as a defect and teach people to ignore the instrument)
reporting divergence only (an identical unlinked copy is still the precondition of tomorrow's rot, so it stays visible, ranked last)
because: the signal a reader cannot get any other way is 'you repeated yourself AND the copies no longer agree' — on this repo that is 24 of 35 pairs, 69% rot, corroborating the shingle measurement that motivated the module

chose: prose floor: Jaccard >= 0.5 over 6-word shingles, sentences >= 12 words, shingle df <= 6, and the render prints a LOWER BOUND line naming what the floor gives up
over: the 0.34 floor the motivating measurement used (more recall: 80 pairs; but the band 0.34-0.5 is where a heavy rewrite and a fresh paraphrase become indistinguishable from text alone, and one false 'defect' on a legitimate summary kills trust in an advisory)
semantic/embedding similarity (could tell paraphrase from copy in principle, but non-deterministic, heavy, and unexplainable in a one-line report)
because: 6-word shingles are already a copy signature — an independent paraphrase almost never reproduces six-word runs — so the floor buys precision and the report says out loud that the copies which drifted FURTHEST are exactly the ones it cannot see, same move as calibration.ts's LOWER BOUND line

chose: prose scans module HEADER essays only, plus non-generated markdown; sentence identity for --raise is file plus a digest of the sentence's own normalized words
over: scanning every comment in a file (inline comments narrate local code; pairing them drowns the reading-surface signal)
keying journal subjects on line numbers or similarity scores (raise.ts doctrine: identity is the addressable subject, nothing volatile)
trying to keep a question's key stable across sentence edits (an edited sentence IS a different sentence — redundancy.ts's stableSiteName makes the same call for alternation sites)
because: the surfaces named by the finding are README, RELEASE-NOTES, spec files and header essays; same-file pairs are excluded because repetition within one document is visible to its reader, and boilerplate stamped into more than maxDf sentences suppresses itself as idiom

chose: the command is named 'prose' with report banner PROSE ROT
over: 'prose-rot' as the command name (the repo's command vocabulary is single surface-nouns: redundancy, economy, mass, atlas; the banner carries the verdict word instead)
because: a command named after its surface stays honest when the report is clean; the rot label belongs to the finding, not the tool

chose: added a one-shared-shingle belowFloor negative control to prose.test.ts after mutation testing showed the paraphrase control was vacuous for the floor
over: trusting the paraphrase control as the floor's refutation (it shares no shingle at all, so it never reaches the floor check — deleting the floor left all pairProse tests green)
because: a negative control that cannot fail under the mutation it claims to guard is the vacuous-green defect this harness hunts; the new control shares exactly one 6-word run and goes red the moment the floor is deleted (verified: mutation b red 6/7, restored green 7/7)

chose: README.md and src/raise.ts hold near-verbatim copies of one sentence that no longer agree
because: A at README.md:1112 reads "The refutation advisory prints its per-invariant list only once a project has declared its first refutation, so on a pr…"; B at src/raise.ts:54 reads "The refutation advisory prints its per-invariant list only once a project has declared its first refutation, so on a pr…" (similarity 0.96 over 6-word shingles). Each copy reads as authoritative on its own, so a reader of one cannot see that the other disagrees — that is rot only a diff can surface, and nothing runs that diff.
couldBe: the instrument is wrong — the thing that PRODUCED this number, not the thing it describes
one side rotted — the argument was updated at one spelling and not at the other, and there was nothing there to notice
the difference is intended — one site deliberately summarizes or re-frames the other, and nobody wrote that down
discriminatedBy: put the two sentences side by side. If one is the stale copy, update or delete it and keep ONE authoritative spelling (derive or reference it — the command-index fix). If the difference is deliberate, dismiss this question saying so.

chose: committed prose.ts, its test, the Config knobs and this journal file only — the cli.ts/commands.ts registration hunks stay uncommitted in the worktree
over: committing src/cli.ts and src/commands.ts too (both carry another agent's unfinished uncommitted splices; a commit of the whole files would publish work that is not mine and not done)
because: the registration is two additive hunks that ride along whenever those files are next committed; the committed state stands alone — the module and its 17 tests pass without the wiring
